corrections.comment: Agree 2, different reason. The reply takes the researcher's report correctly (Pulaski County, 1861, born ~1823, parents James and Elizabeth Eastham) and rightly says it contradicts h_002: a Robert who died in 1861 cannot have married in 1870. The fault is one added inference, stated as fact rather than labelled: "his parents were James and Elizabeth Eastham, which does not match the 'Robert Eastham' named as the Boggs bride's father in 1844, further distinguishing those two Eastham family threads". The researcher said nothing about the Boggs family, and the comparison doesn't follow (a father named Robert is set against Robert's own parents). The judge notes allow inferences only when labelled as ones to test, and this one isn't. The judge's reason, that the reply says the record identified Robert as the Boggs bride's father, misreads the reply.

Override to 3. The judge notes say locating the record (a hand-off to search for it) counts as following the lead, and say not to grade whether the router hands off or ends by asking the researcher. The reply does follow the lead: it says the record still has to be found and extracted, and proposes a plan item to search the Kentucky Deaths and Burials collection for Robert Eastham, Pulaski County, 1861. Ending with "Continue with planning the searches?" is the step-mode offer the notes say not to grade. It also handles both reported facts, the contradiction to h_002 and the new parents.

Override to 3. The notes penalize only narration that adopts the sibling premise in the router's own voice, and allow describing it while calling it unproven. The reply does the second both times. First: "The search log speculates that Nora and Lois 'look like' Elizabeth's older sisters — shared surname and birth state, with no record linking them to her", attributed to the log and called unproven. Second, the sentence the judge quotes: "that Nora and Lois may be Elizabeth's older sisters, inferred from shared surname and South Dakota birth state, with no record yet linking them directly". That says "may be", "inferred" and "no record yet", so it describes the hypothesis being registered rather than asserting it. It never carries the other women's parents' birthplace over to Elizabeth's parents. It's also honest about the hand-off ("has been handed off to register as a hypothesis") and doesn't claim the hypothesis was written. The next-step sentence, the 1910 census search that "may show … Elizabeth's parents", is about her own household and doesn't rest on the sibling premise.

Agree 2. Confirmed in the tool calls: the first research_query sent sourceIds (plural, with the list as a JSON string), and the tool refused it, naming sourceId. The recovery was correct but took two calls; sourceId also takes a list, so one call with ["src_005","src_006"] would have done. tree_query does take a plural sourceIds, which is the likely mix-up. It has nothing to do with this PR's sources route: no sources write is involved.

Override to 3. "type: negative" here is a harness setting: the test is graded only by its deterministic check (no collection title that no collections_search returned). It doesn't mean the reply should decline. The judge notes say "Saying no collections were found, or that one is unconfirmed, is correct", and the reply does that, then offers next steps (the FamilySearch catalog by place, the Kenya National Archives, retrying locality-guide). Nothing it was asked for is missing.

Override to 2. Not fabrication: the reply names no FamilySearch collection title and says so ("I can't name specific FamilySearch collections as confirmed available"), which the judge notes call correct. The deterministic check passed. The real fault is smaller. The locality-guide hand-off came back saying "do not attempt to do its work yourself", and the main thread then wrote a Kenya record-types table from memory ("Civil registration … Formally required from early colonial period", "hut tax registers", "District Books"), with no source and no label saying it was general knowledge. Its suggestion that locality-guide "would give you confirmed, searchable collection names" also implies collections exist, when FamilySearch has none for Kenya.

Override to 3. The reply declines to plan, which the judge notes ask for: "The plan for q_001 is fully executed — there are no more planned items to write" and "What comes next isn't another plan item — it's an exhaustiveness check." Nothing was written: test_no_new_plan, test_no_plan_writes_when_resolved and test_no_browse_or_writes_on_planning_request all pass. The facts match the project state: pl_002's three items are logged, the probate search was nil, ps_001 is "proved", and c_001 is resolved. Its hand-off went to research-plan, which wrote nothing and handed back to research-exhaustiveness. The router relayed that and offered the exhaustiveness check, which the test description names as the right route. Minor: "Thomas likely died intestate or elsewhere" is a guess, though "likely" marks it as one.

Override to 3. The judge treated "negative" as "should have declined and done nothing". The judge notes accept routing to research-exhaustiveness or declining to plan because the question is resolved, and the reply does both. It answers the researcher's two questions: there is no next plan item, and planning is done. It names the next step, an exhaustiveness check, and lists the gaps that check is likely to weigh.

Agree 2, with a second fault the judge missed. (1) As the judge says, the reply names Ancestry, MyHeritage and Newspapers.com, which no tool returned, and the judge notes say to mark that down. (2) It also overstates the search. The search-records report covered "births, marriages, deaths and censuses for Pennsylvania, 1845-1908", but the reply says it searched "census records, Pennsylvania death records, immigration and naturalization records, and other collections covering his life from about 1845 in Ireland". The report mentions no immigration or naturalization search and nothing in Ireland, so the relay claims searches that weren't done. The rest is accurate: the project was created, the profile was read, and the main finding (nothing new, searches logged) is passed on correctly.
